sentences.text:
The suit filed by plaintiff against defendant for recovery of a sum of Rs. 9,61,594/- along with interest at the rate of 24%.
2. The brief facts of the plaintiff is as under :-
The plaintiff on the application of the defendant has sanctioned and disbursed a loan of Rs 7,50,000/- on 16.05.2017.
The said loan was to be repaid 85 Equal Monthly Installments of Rs 12,219.61/- starting from 30.06.2017 till 30.01.2020.
The defendant has executed Hypothecation cum loan agreement dated 16.05.2017 along with other documents for a sum of Rs 7,50,000/-.
In pursuance of the sanction of the loan amount the defendant has deposited margin money of Rs 2,20,000/-.
Thereafter the plaintiff Bank issued a Demand draft dated 167.05.2017 for a sum of Rs 9,65,607/-.

The defendant after taking the delivery of the vehicle bearing Regn. No. KA 02 MM 5034 has not produced the vehicle for the inspection of the Branch Officials and has failed to create hypothecation in favour of plaintiff Bank.
The defendant had agreed to repay the loan amount with interest at the rate of 9.3 % p.a. with monthly rests, also agreed to pay overdue interest of Rs 2% p.a.
The defendant became chronic defaulter and failed to pay the installments though Bank issued reminders time and again.
The plaintiff also issued seizure notice dated 28.11.2017 calling upon the defendant to regularize the account on or before 31.12.2017.

The plaintiff addressed an email dated 07.09.2018 to M/s. Advaith Hyundai Pvt. Ltd and sought for the details of the vehicle and also sought for details of the person to whom it was delivered and M/s Advaith Hyundai vide its email dated 08.09.2018 confirmed that the vehicle was delivered to the defendant, however the Chassis number given by them was different from what was provided by the defendant.
The plaintiff applied for B-extract of the vehicle and found that vehicle was transferred by the defendant in favour of one Ayesha Nazeen without obtaining NOC from the Bank.

The plaintiff filed a complaint against the defendant with Chennammanekere Achukatti Police on 18.10.2018, the police registered FIR vide Cr. No. 314/2018 against the defendant for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
Even after the registration of the FIR and issuance of number of notice to the defendant he has not come forward to clear the dues.
Plaintiff issued yet another legal notice to the defendant.
However the same was not served upon the defendant and was returned with postal shara address insufficient.
Hence the present suit.
3. The defendant after service of summons by way of paper publication in daily news paper has not appeared and hence he is placed exparte.
4. The plaintiff in order to prove its case against defendants got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked Ex. P.1 to P.14 documents.

5. The points that arise for my consideration are as follows:-
1. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief as prayed in this suit ?
2. What Order?
6. Having heard the argument and perusing of the materials on record, my answer to the above points are:-
Point No.1 :- Partly in the Affirmative.

Point No.2 :- As per final order for the following :-
REASONS 7. Point No.1:-

The Authorized Officer of Plaintiff Bank who is examined as P.W.1 has stated in his evidence that on the application of the defendant has sanctioned and disbursed a loan of Rs 7,50,000/- on 16.05.2017.
The said loan was to be repaid 85 Equal Monthly Installments of Rs 12,219.61/- starting from 30.06.2017 till 30.01.2020.
The defendant has executed Hypothecation cum loan agreement dated 16.05.2017 along with other documents for a sum of Rs 7,50,000/-.
In pursuance of the sanction of the loan amount the defendant has deposited margin money of Rs 2,20,000/-.
Thereafter the plaintiff Bank issued a Demand draft dated 167.05.2017 for a sum of Rs 9,65,607/-.

The defendant after taking the delivery of the vehicle bearing Regn. No. KA 02 MM 5034 has not produced the vehicle for the inspection of the Branch Officials and has failed to create hypothecation in favour of plaintiff Bank.
The defendant had agreed to repay the loan amount with interest at the rate of 9.3 % p.a. with monthly rests, also agreed to pay overdue interest of Rs 2% p.a.
The defendant became chronic defaulter and failed to pay the installments though Bank issued reminders time and again.
The plaintiff also issued seizure notice dated 28.11.2017 calling upon the defendant to regularize the account on or before 31.12.2017.

The plaintiff addressed an email dated 07.09.2018 to M/s. Advaith Hyundai Pvt. Ltd and sought for the details of the vehicle and also sought for details of the person to whom it was delivered and M/s Advaith Hyundai vide its email dated 08.09.2018 confirmed that the vehicle was delivered to the defendant, however the Chassis number given by them was different from what was provided by the defendant.
The plaintiff applied for B-extract of the vehicle and found that vehicle was transferred by the defendant in favour of one Ayesha Nazeen without obtaining NOC from the Bank.

The plaintiff filed a complaint against the defendant with Chennammanekere Achukatti Police on 18.10.2018, the police registered FIR vide Cr. No. 314/2018 against the defendant for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
Even after the registration of the FIR and issuance of number of notice to the defendant he has not come forward to clear the dues.
Plaintiff issued yet another legal notice to the defendant.
However the same was not served upon the defendant and was returned with postal shara address insufficient.
8. The plaintiff in support of his case produced Ex.P.1 to P.14 documents - Ex.P.1
Original identity card and self attested ID card, Ex.P.2 account statement, Ex.P.3 loan application dated 16.5.2017,

Ex.P.4 sanction letter dated 16.05.2017, Ex.P.5 loan agreement dated 16.05.2017, Ex.P.6 Invoice dated 09.05.2017, Ex.P.7 ASD 13 (confirmation of delivery of title), Ex.P.8 E-mail exchanged M/S Canara Bank vs Ravi on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54533766/
3 between plaintiff and Hyundai, Ex.P.9 Copy of complaint, Ex.P.10 legal notice dated 24.04.2020,
Ex.P.11 Postal receipt, Ex.P.12 Postal unserved cover, Ex.P.13 Certificate u/s 2 (a) (b) and 2 (a) (c) of Bankers' Book Evidence Act and Ex.P.14 Authorization letter dated 24.02.2025.
9.
The plaintiff has claimed total amount of Rs. 9,61,594/- along with interest at the rate of 24%.
The rate of interest claimed by the plaintiff is on higher side.

Therefore, the plaintiff is entitled 10%
interest on the total amount claimed.
Inspite of service of summons through paper publication, the defendant has not appeared before the Court to deny the amount claimed by the plaintiff.
Hence, the defendant is placed exparte.
The plaintiff by leading oral and documentary evidence has proved his case against the defendant.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 partly in the Affirmative.

10. Point No.2:- In view of the above discussion on Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following order:-
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is decreed partly with cost.

The plaintiff shall recover an amount of Rs. 9,61,594/- along with interest at the rate of 10.00 % per annum on the said amount till the date of realization by deducting the amount if any paid by the defendant.

The defendant is granted three months time to pay the decreed amount, failing which the plaintiff is at liberty to recover the decreed amount from the person and properties of defendant.
Draw decree accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer online, typed by him, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 12th day of March 2025.)
(Laxman Ramu Kurane)
XV Addl.City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru.
